data.name: Ratiyah
data.gender_notes: Ratiyah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic root 'r-t-y', meaning 'to be satisfied' or 'contented'. It reflects a sense of inner peace and joy,. It is also said to be a name of a companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and a wife of Ibrahim (Abraham) in Islamic tradition. The name Ratiyah carries the meaning “Contented, Satisfied” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ratiyah usually hope their child will grow to embody contented, satisfied and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name with deep spiritual significance, reflecting a state of contentment and satisfaction with one's life and faith. It is also associated with the companions of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the wife of Ibrahim (Abraham) in Islamic tradition.
data.etymology: Ratiyah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Contented, Satisfied.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ratiyah total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ratiyah" carries rich cultural symbolism in the Islamic world. It represents a person who is satisfied and contented, an admirable trait in Islamic teachings. This name reflects a strong connection to the Islamic belief in inner peace and tranquility, which is an essential goal for every Muslim. The name can be given to both boys and girls, making it a versatile and meaningful choice.
data.spiritual_significance: "Ratiyah" is a spiritual name that resonates with the inner calm and satisfaction that comes from experiencing the love and mercy of Allah. It reminds us of the hadith, "contentment is the foundation of faith," and encourages us to seek inner peace and tranquility. The name invites us to focus on the present moment and recognize the blessings that surround us, bringing us closer to Allah and His divine wisdom. It is a beautiful reminder of the importance of being spiritually fulfilled and contented, no matter what the external circumstances might be.
